findings.reason: without the write site named, the node can land the behaviour and still leave §8's query with no field to read, and §8 has no way to detect that.
findings.text: §4 names its two read sites precisely (the seeder at `_worker_fence.py:317` and the argv in `_ClaudeDialect`) but the third mechanism it depends on — writing `anchored_edit` plus its reason onto the run record — names no writer, while §8's entire population split is taken from that field; the nearest carrier is the launched-worker record at `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2938`, which records `"fenced"` the same way and is the site the node would have to find unaided

findings.reason: the node is asked to build and gate a feature whose contract may be recorded as unsettled, and §7's done-when tests no resume case, so the gap would land as untested code rather than as a blocker.
findings.text: §7's deliverable lists `resume` among what it builds on what §6 settled, but §6's done-when makes only three items mandatory (event-stream format, one endpoint prompt, the per-run switches) and explicitly allows the remaining two — of which resume is one — to be "answered or marked unsettled with the reason", so §7 is licensed to proceed on a contract that may not describe resume at all
